story.text: The phrase is usually traced to a line in the household maxims of the late-Ming, early-Qing scholar Zhu Yongchun: for every bowl of porridge and every meal, remember that it did not come easily; for every half thread of silk, keep in mind how hard material things are to produce.
story.source: 朱用纯《治家格言》（《朱子家训》）：一粥一饭，当思来处不易

use.how: Predicate or attributive with 的: 这份成绩来之不易 / 来之不易的机会. Said of a result, chance or possession already gained, usually implying it should be valued.

near.diff: 千辛万苦 describes the hardships themselves; 来之不易 describes the result they produced and implies it must be cherished.

cue: After years of saving, a couple finally buys a small flat and tells their son to take good care of it. How do they describe the flat?

ctx.s: 这份工作{来之不易}，你要好好珍惜。
ctx.en: This job wasn't easy to get; you should value it.

ctx.s: 妈妈常说，每一粒米都{来之不易}，不要浪费。
ctx.en: Mum always says every grain of rice comes at a cost, so don't waste it.

ctx.s: 这场胜利{来之不易}，全队整整练了一年。
ctx.en: This victory was hard-won; the whole team trained for a full year.

ctx.s: 他把这笔{来之不易}的奖学金全部用来买书了。
ctx.en: He spent the whole of that hard-earned scholarship on books.

ctx.s: “你知道这次机会是多么{来之不易}吗？”
ctx.en: "Do you know how hard this chance was to come by?"

ctx.s: 两家公司谈了半年才签下合同，双方都明白这次合作{来之不易}。
ctx.en: The two companies negotiated for six months before signing; both sides know this partnership was hard-won.

bad.s: 这道数学题{来之不易}，我做了一个小时也没做出来。
bad.en: (meant: this maths problem is hard)
bad.why: It describes something already obtained through effort, not a task that is hard to do; just say the problem is hard.

bad.s: 他今天{来之不易}，路上堵了两个小时。
bad.en: (meant: it was hard for him to get here today)
bad.why: It is not about a person physically arriving; it is said of results, chances or possessions won with effort.

use.how: Adverbial (日复一日地练习) or attributive (日复一日的生活). Stresses the same thing repeated over a long stretch, often monotonous; pairs with 年复一年.

near.diff: 久而久之 introduces the result that a long time brings; 日复一日 stresses the sameness of each repeated day.

cue: A night watchman describes walking the same corridors and checking the same doors every night for twenty years. How does he describe his routine?

ctx.s: 他{日复一日}地练习写字，从来没停过。
ctx.en: He practised his handwriting day after day and never stopped.

ctx.s: 这种{日复一日}的生活让他觉得很无聊。
ctx.en: This same-every-day life bores him.

ctx.s: 老人{日复一日}地守着这家小店，一守就是三十年。
ctx.en: Day after day the old man kept watch over his little shop, for thirty years.

ctx.s: “你不觉得{日复一日}做同样的事很累吗？”
ctx.en: "Don't you find it tiring doing the same thing day after day?"

ctx.s: 时间就在这样{日复一日}的等待中过去了。
ctx.en: Time slipped away in this waiting, day after day.

ctx.s: 环卫工人{日复一日}、年复一年地清扫着这条街。
ctx.en: Day after day, year after year, the street cleaners sweep this street.

bad.s: 我{日复一日}去了一次超市。
bad.en: (meant: I went to the supermarket once today)
bad.why: It describes something repeated over a long time; it cannot describe a single event or mean 'today'.

bad.s: 明天开始，我们{日复一日}见面吧！
bad.en: (meant: from tomorrow, let's meet every day)
bad.why: It narrates long, often tedious repetition; it is not a neutral 'every day' for making plans or suggestions.

use.how: Clause-initial connective, usually followed by a comma: 久而久之，… Introduces the outcome that a habit or situation produces after a long time.

near.diff: 日复一日 dwells on the repetition itself; 久而久之 links that repetition to what it eventually leads to.

cue: You chat with a neighbour over the fence every evening, and a year later you have become close friends. How do you link the habit to the result?

ctx.s: 他每天读一点中文报纸，{久而久之}，阅读速度快了很多。
ctx.en: He read a little of a Chinese newspaper every day, and over time his reading got much faster.

ctx.s: 她总是不吃早饭，{久而久之}，胃就出了问题。
ctx.en: She kept skipping breakfast, and eventually her stomach started giving her trouble.

ctx.s: 两个人天天一起上下班，{久而久之}就成了好朋友。
ctx.en: The two of them commuted together every day and, over time, became good friends.

ctx.s: 谎话说多了，{久而久之}，连他自己都信了。
ctx.en: He told the lie so often that in time even he believed it.

ctx.s: “别小看这些坏习惯，{久而久之}会影响健康的。”
ctx.en: "Don't underestimate these bad habits; over time they'll affect your health."

ctx.s: 公司里没人敢提意见，{久而久之}，问题越积越多。
ctx.en: No one at the company dared to speak up, and over time the problems piled up.

bad.s: 我等了他{久而久之}，他还没来。
bad.en: (meant: I waited for him a long time)
bad.why: It is not a duration phrase placed after a verb; it is a connective that introduces a gradual result.

bad.s: {久而久之}以前，这里是一片农田。
bad.en: (meant: long ago this was farmland)
bad.why: It does not mean 'long ago'. It links a long process to its outcome.

mean: let's not put it off; better get going right away (urging action)
lit: the matter should not be delayed

use.how: A clause on its own, followed by what to do now: 事不宜迟，我们马上出发。 Said by someone urging immediate action on a particular matter.

near.diff: 刻不容缓 describes a situation as extremely urgent (这件事刻不容缓); 事不宜迟 is the speaker's call to start right now.

cue: Concert tickets go on sale in ten minutes and your friend is still chatting. You stand up and say: no more dawdling, let's go and queue.

ctx.s: {事不宜迟}，我们现在就出发吧。
ctx.en: No time to lose; let's set off now.

ctx.s: 票快卖完了，{事不宜迟}，赶紧下单！
ctx.en: The tickets are nearly sold out. Don't wait, order now!

ctx.s: 天快下雨了，{事不宜迟}，咱们得赶紧把衣服收进来。
ctx.en: It's about to rain; we'd better get the washing in right away.

ctx.s: 医生看完片子说：“{事不宜迟}，明天就安排手术。”
ctx.en: After looking at the scans the doctor said: "We shouldn't delay. We'll schedule the operation for tomorrow."

ctx.s: 既然大家都同意了，{事不宜迟}，我们今天下午就开始准备。
ctx.en: Since everyone agrees, let's not put it off; we start preparing this afternoon.

ctx.s: 他心想：{事不宜迟}，于是放下电话就去了银行。
ctx.en: He thought: no point waiting. He went to the bank as soon as he hung up.

bad.s: 这家餐厅上菜太慢了，真是{事不宜迟}。
bad.en: (meant: this restaurant is far too slow)
bad.why: It urges acting now; it is not a complaint that something is slow or late.

bad.s: 他做事总是{事不宜迟}，从不拖拉。
bad.en: (meant: he always acts promptly)
bad.why: It is not a description of someone's habits; it is said about one matter that calls for action now.

mean: unable to hold back one's feelings
lit: feelings one cannot restrain in oneself

use.how: Adverbial before a verb, often with 地: 情不自禁地笑了起来. Describes an involuntary reaction driven by emotion: laughing, crying, singing, cheering.

near.diff: 不由自主 covers any action one can't control, even physical ones (腿不由自主地发抖); 情不自禁 is always driven by emotion.

cue: At your daughter's first school concert you are on your feet clapping and cheering before you have even decided to. How did you react?

ctx.s: 听到这个好消息，她{情不自禁}地笑了。
ctx.en: Hearing the good news, she couldn't help smiling.

ctx.s: 音乐一响，孩子们{情不自禁}地跟着跳了起来。
ctx.en: As soon as the music started, the children couldn't help dancing along.

ctx.s: 看到老照片，奶奶{情不自禁}流下了眼泪。
ctx.en: Looking at the old photos, Grandma couldn't hold back her tears.

ctx.s: “对不起，刚才看比赛太激动了，我{情不自禁}就喊出声来了。”
ctx.en: "Sorry, I got so excited watching the match that I shouted out without meaning to."

ctx.s: 站在山顶看日出的那一刻，我们都{情不自禁}地欢呼起来。
ctx.en: The moment we watched the sunrise from the summit, we all burst into cheers.

ctx.s: 听到自己的名字，她激动得{情不自禁}地抱住了身边的教练。
ctx.en: Hearing her name called, she was so overcome that she threw her arms around her coach.

bad.s: 冬天太冷，我{情不自禁}地发抖。
bad.en: (meant: it was so cold I shivered)
bad.why: Shivering from cold is physical, not emotional; the idiom needs a feeling as the cause.

bad.s: 他是个很{情不自禁}的人，经常发脾气。
bad.en: (meant: he is a man who can't control his temper)
bad.why: It is not an adjective for someone's character; it describes one moment's involuntary reaction and goes before a verb.

lit: one's gall is as small as a mouse (the gallbladder is the seat of courage)

use.how: Predicate describing a person's character: 他胆小如鼠. Mocking or contemptuous; not for a reasonable fear in one situation.

near.diff: 胆战心惊 is a moment of intense fear; 胆小如鼠 labels a lasting cowardly character.

cue: A man boasts that nothing scares him, then runs off at the sight of a small puppy and won't walk down a dark stairwell. How do you mock him?

ctx.s: 别看他个子高，其实{胆小如鼠}。
ctx.en: He may be tall, but he's actually a real coward.

ctx.s: 他{胆小如鼠}，连晚上一个人回家都不敢。
ctx.en: He's such a scaredy-cat he won't even walk home alone at night.

ctx.s: “一只小虫子就把你吓跑了，真是{胆小如鼠}！”
ctx.en: "A tiny bug sent you running. What a scaredy-cat!"

ctx.s: 我小时候{胆小如鼠}，一打雷就躲进被子里。
ctx.en: As a kid I was a total scaredy-cat; at the first clap of thunder I'd hide under the covers.

ctx.s: 他嘴上说什么都不怕，一遇到事却{胆小如鼠}，躲得比谁都快。
ctx.en: He says he fears nothing, but when trouble comes he's a coward and hides faster than anyone.

ctx.s: 故事里的那个国王{胆小如鼠}，一听说要打仗就躲进了宫里。
ctx.en: The king in the story was a coward; at the first word of war he hid in his palace.

bad.s: 他开车{胆小如鼠}，所以从来没出过事故。
bad.en: (meant: he drives cautiously, so he's never had an accident)
bad.why: It is contemptuous, calling someone a coward; it is not praise for caution.

bad.s: 第一次上台演讲，我有点{胆小如鼠}。
bad.en: (meant: giving my first speech, I was a bit nervous)
bad.why: It labels a cowardly character and can't be softened into 'a bit' to describe one-off stage nerves.

use.how: Predicate or adverbial: 别疑神疑鬼的 / 整天疑神疑鬼. Criticises someone who suspects people or things without real grounds.

near.diff: 草木皆兵 is panic after a fright that sees enemies everywhere; 疑神疑鬼 is groundless suspicion and worry in everyday life.

cue: Your flatmate is sure someone read her diary because her pen was moved, and now checks the lock five times every night. What do you tell her to stop doing?

ctx.s: 别{疑神疑鬼}的，门是你自己锁好的。
ctx.en: Stop imagining things; you locked the door yourself.

ctx.s: 他最近总是{疑神疑鬼}，觉得同事在背后说他坏话。
ctx.en: Lately he's been paranoid, convinced his colleagues talk about him behind his back.

ctx.s: “手机响一下你就{疑神疑鬼}，到底在担心什么？”
ctx.en: "Every time the phone buzzes you get suspicious. What are you actually worried about?"

ctx.s: 一个人住久了，她晚上听到一点声音就{疑神疑鬼}。
ctx.en: After living alone so long, the slightest sound at night sets her imagining things.

ctx.s: 老板{疑神疑鬼}地把每份报销单都查了三遍。
ctx.en: The boss, suspicious of everyone, checked every expense claim three times.

ctx.s: 丈夫晚回家半小时，她就开始{疑神疑鬼}，一个接一个地打电话。
ctx.en: When her husband was half an hour late she started imagining the worst and made call after call.

bad.s: 警察{疑神疑鬼}地调查了现场，终于找到了小偷。
bad.en: (meant: the police searched the scene carefully and caught the thief)
bad.why: It criticises groundless suspicion; it cannot describe careful, justified investigation.

bad.s: 这座老房子{疑神疑鬼}，大家都说里面有鬼。
bad.en: (meant: this old house is spooky)
bad.why: It describes a person's suspicious state of mind, not a place that seems haunted.

lit: a true heart and a real intention

use.how: Adverbial with 地 (真心实意地帮助), predicate, or noun (我们的真心实意). Said of a person's sincerity towards others.

near.diff: 全心全意 is giving all one's effort and devotion; 真心实意 is meaning it, not faking it.

cue: Your neighbour has helped you move house three times and never once expected anything in return. How do you describe his help?

ctx.s: 他是{真心实意}想帮你，不是为了钱。
ctx.en: He genuinely wants to help you; it's not about money.

ctx.s: 我{真心实意}地向你道歉，请你原谅我。
ctx.en: I sincerely apologise to you; please forgive me.

ctx.s: 交朋友要{真心实意}，不能只想着自己。
ctx.en: To make friends you have to be sincere, not just think of yourself.

ctx.s: “你这话是{真心实意}的，还是客气客气？”
ctx.en: "Do you really mean that, or are you just being polite?"

ctx.s: 老师对学生的关心是{真心实意}的，从来不做表面文章。
ctx.en: The teacher's care for the students is genuine; it's never just for show.

ctx.s: 客户最后签了合同，因为他们感受到了我们的{真心实意}。
ctx.en: The client finally signed because they could feel our sincerity.

bad.s: 这件衣服的质量很{真心实意}。
bad.en: (meant: this garment is of genuine quality)
bad.why: It describes a person's sincerity, not the authenticity or quality of goods.

bad.s: 他{真心实意}地骗了我。
bad.en: (meant: he really did deceive me)
bad.why: Sincerity contradicts deceit; it is not an intensifier meaning 'really'.

lit: to put on a pattern and make a show

use.how: Predicate or adverbial with 地: 装模作样地看书 / 别装模作样了. Criticises pretending: a show without the real feeling or activity behind it.

near.diff: 装腔作势 is putting on airs to impress or intimidate; 装模作样 is any pretence, such as faking busyness or feelings.

cue: A student playing games on his phone hears the teacher's footsteps, quickly opens a textbook and frowns at it. What is he doing?

ctx.s: 老师一进来，他就{装模作样}地看起书来。
ctx.en: As soon as the teacher came in, he made a show of reading.

ctx.s: 别{装模作样}了，我知道你根本没睡着。
ctx.en: Stop pretending; I know you're not asleep at all.

ctx.s: 他根本不懂画，却{装模作样}地在画前站了半天。
ctx.en: He knows nothing about painting, yet he stood in front of it for ages putting on an act.

ctx.s: “你又不是真想帮忙，何必{装模作样}？”
ctx.en: "You don't really want to help, so why the act?"

ctx.s: 她{装模作样}地叹了口气，其实心里高兴得很。
ctx.en: She gave a theatrical sigh, though inside she was delighted.

ctx.s: 弟弟偷吃了蛋糕，还{装模作样}地问妈妈蛋糕去哪儿了。
ctx.en: My little brother ate the cake, then innocently asked Mum where it had gone.

bad.s: 演员在舞台上{装模作样}，演得特别好。
bad.en: (meant: the actor performed brilliantly on stage)
bad.why: It is derogatory, for faking in real life; it is not praise for acting a role.

bad.s: 为了参加婚礼，她{装模作样}地化了妆。
bad.en: (meant: she did her make-up nicely for the wedding)
bad.why: It is not about dressing up; it means pretending to a feeling or activity one does not really have.

mean: to think oneself clever and act on it
lit: to make oneself out to be clever

use.how: Predicate or adverbial: 别自作聪明 / 他自作聪明地改了计划. Criticises acting on one's own clever idea without asking, usually with a bad result.

near.diff: 弄巧成拙 names the outcome, a clever trick that backfires; 自作聪明 criticises the attitude of acting on one's own supposed cleverness.
画蛇添足 is spoiling something by adding the unnecessary; 自作聪明 is any self-confident 'clever' move made without asking, often a change or shortcut.

cue: Without asking anyone, a colleague 'improves' the file format the client requested, and now the client's software can't open it. What did he do?

ctx.s: 别{自作聪明}，按说明书做就行。
ctx.en: Don't try to be clever; just follow the instructions.

ctx.s: 他{自作聪明}地改了密码，结果自己也忘了。
ctx.en: He thought he was being clever changing the password, and then forgot it himself.

ctx.s: “谁让你{自作聪明}的？客户要的就是原来的设计。”
ctx.en: "Who told you to get clever? The client wanted the original design."

ctx.s: 我{自作聪明}抄了近路，结果迷了路，比平时晚到了一个小时。
ctx.en: I thought I'd be smart and take a shortcut, got lost, and arrived an hour later than usual.

ctx.s: 实习生{自作聪明}，删掉了报告里他觉得没用的部分。
ctx.en: The intern decided he knew best and deleted the parts of the report he thought were useless.

ctx.s: 故事里的狐狸总爱{自作聪明}，最后掉进了自己挖的坑。
ctx.en: The fox in the story was too clever for its own good and ended up falling into the pit it had dug.

bad.s: 她{自作聪明}，考试总是得第一名。
bad.en: (meant: she is clever and always comes first)
bad.why: It mocks misplaced cleverness; it is never praise for real intelligence.

bad.s: 这个问题太难，我得{自作聪明}地想一想。
bad.en: (meant: this is hard, I need to think it through on my own)
bad.why: It does not mean thinking for oneself; it criticises an ill-judged action already taken or about to be.
